key_insight: AI can now produce seizure research manuscripts, peer reviews, and editorial decisions that often look convincing enough to challenge human detection.
clinical_relevance: This raises publication-governance concerns for medical research, suggesting AI can support drafting and review but should not be left to make unsupervised scientific decisions.
method: 3 epileptologists each created one AI-fabricated seizure manuscript based on a published Epilepsia paper.
AI tools were then used to simulate peer review and editorial decisions with minimal human oversight.
Researchers compared AI-fabricated vs human-written papers and recorded epileptologists’ ability to identify them.
evidence_signal: Epileptologists correctly identified 4 of 6 AI-fabricated vs human manuscript pairs (67%), and only 1 AI-fabricated manuscript was rejected by AI editorial review.
watch_item: A key concern is that AI-generated academic content may appear high-quality and authoritative while still being fabricated, so human oversight and policy guardrails are essential.
paper_title: Full stack academic publishing in seizures with artificial intelligence: a cautionary tale
